notes.system: Template-owned. Replaced wholesale by sidecar-update.yml on every upstream release. The engine under bot/ lives here so users receive fixes to it — but the engine is INERT: nothing in the template calls it, and AGENTS.md names no part of it, so a delivered engine update cannot change what a cycle does. Only the user's own LOOP_PROMPT.md can invoke it.
notes.system_setup: Onboarding files, replaced only while the repo is still UNINITIALIZED — same setup-token test as system_if_uninitialized, read off LOOP_PROMPT.md. Once setup has filled the mandate in, these are finished business: an interview you already answered and a SETUP.md you already followed are not worth a PR every release. They are skipped and named in the PR body, so a repo past onboarding can decline them without declining engine fixes.
notes.system_if_uninitialized: Template-owned only while the file still contains real {{TOKEN}} markers (the rail greps for specific setup tokens like {{ACCOUNT_ID}}, not a blanket '{{' — templates mention {{PLACEHOLDER}} in prose). Once setup fills it, the file is the user's and is never touched again — it is skipped and named in the update PR instead. Only FILL-IN TEMPLATES belong here: a file that is written once and then owned. A file that ACCUMULATES content belongs in system_if_absent — see the note there.
notes.system_if_absent: Delivered ONLY when the file does not exist, and never touched again — the check is existence, not content. JOURNAL.md and DECISIONS.md accumulate: a user appends to them for months. Token-gating them was a data-loss bug (fixed 1.7.1). The gate asks 'does this still contain a placeholder', which for an accumulating file answers 'yes' for as long as any one token in its header goes unfilled — so a journal with two months of real entries and a single {{AUTONOMY}} left in its standing-rules block was replaced wholesale by the 40-line seed, under a PR body promising the journal was untouched. Existence is the only safe test for these. bot/state.json and bot/failures.jsonl are here for the same reason and a second one: state.json is the engine's live record of positions, entry dates and clocks, so a fresh clone needs the empty template ONCE and a running instance must never receive it again.
notes.user: Never touched by tooling. README.md is here because an instance that wrote its own README lost it on every update while this file listed it under system — a live bug until this release. JOURNAL.md, DECISIONS.md, LOOP_PROMPT.md, bot/state.json and bot/failures.jsonl appear here and in a system class; the ownership test resolves the overlap — placeholder tokens for LOOP_PROMPT.md, existence for the rest. bot/raw/ and bot/brief.md are gitignored broker data and are listed only to say, in writing, that nothing upstream will ever write them.
notes.not_delivered: tools/, tests/ and docs/ROADMAP.md are deliberately in NO class. tools/ and tests/ are maintainer CI for the template repo itself: tools/secret_scan.py fails a build on anything shaped like a real account number, which is correct upstream and wrong in a private clone whose LOOP_PROMPT.md legitimately contains one. docs/ROADMAP.md is a maintainer planning doc that says so in its own header and is not read by agents during cycles. .github/workflows/ci.yml is likewise unlisted and additionally guarded on the repository name. Anything else appearing here is an oversight — tests/test_manifest.py fails on a tracked file that is in no class and on no exclusion list.
notes.workflow: .github/workflows/sidecar-update.yml cannot update itself (GITHUB_TOKEN may not push workflow-file changes). When the rail changes upstream, the update PR body flags it as a one-file manual copy.
